alternate_titles: Simulation Modeling for AI Rack Landing in Large Scale Datacenters
papers.abstract: The planning for AI hardware deployments is driven by the evolving demands of products and services. High-performing AI servers play an important role in supporting AI and ML workloads across these platforms. In this paper, we present a case study on the application of Monte Carlo simulations for AI rack landing. The reliable planning and allocation of high-performing AI servers are particularly important in large scale datacenters, which consist of diverse hardware types, components and software systems that work together to support the execution of various AI models and applications. This study helps understand the application Monte Carlo simulations to forecast rack landing quantities and support efficient deployment. papers.title: Preserving Full Degradation Details for Blind Image Super-Resolution
alternate_titles: Preserving Full Degradation Details for Blind Image Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: The performance of image super-resolution relies heavily on the accuracy of degradation information, especially under blind settings. Due to the absence of true degradation models in real-world scenarios, previous methods learn distinct representations by distinguishing different degradations in a batch. However, the most significant degradation differences may provide shortcuts for the learning of representations such that subtle difference may be discarded. In this paper, we propose an alternative to learn degradation representations through reproducing degraded low-resolution (LR) images. By guiding the degrader to reconstruct input LR images, full degradation information can be encoded into the representations. In addition, we develop a distribution alignment loss to facilitate the learning of the degradation representations by introducing a bounded constraint. Moreover, to achieve l...

papers.title: Evaluating Knowledge-based Cross-lingual Inconsistency in Large Language Models
alternate_titles: Evaluating Knowledge-based Cross-lingual Inconsistency in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the cross-lingual inconsistencies observed in Large Language Models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, Llama, and Baichuan, which have shown exceptional performance in various Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks. Despite their successes, these models often exhibit significant inconsistencies when processing the same concepts across different languages. This study focuses on three primary questions: the existence of cross-lingual inconsistencies in LLMs, the specific aspects in which these inconsistencies manifest, and the correlation between cross-lingual consistency and multilingual capabilities of LLMs.To address these questions, we propose an innovative evaluation method for Cross-lingual Semantic Consistency (xSC) using the LaBSE model. alternate_titles: Complementary Fusion of Deep Network and Tree Model for ETA Prediction
papers.abstract: Estimated time of arrival (ETA) is a very important factor in the transportation system. It has attracted increasing attentions and has been widely used as a basic service in navigation systems and intelligent transportation systems. In this paper, we propose a novel solution to the ETA estimation problem, which is an ensemble on tree models and neural networks. We proved the accuracy and robustness of the solution on the A/B list and finally won first place in the SIGSPATIAL 2021 GISCUP competition.

papers.title: CLEME2.0: Towards Interpretable Evaluation by Disentangling Edits for Grammatical Error Correction
alternate_titles: CLEME2.0: Towards Interpretable Evaluation by Disentangling Edits for Grammatical Error Correction
papers.abstract: The paper focuses on the interpretability of Grammatical Error Correction (GEC) evaluation metrics, which received little attention in previous studies. To bridge the gap, we introduce **CLEME2.0**, a reference-based metric describing four fundamental aspects of GEC systems: hit-correction, wrong-correction, under-correction, and over-correction. They collectively contribute to exposing critical qualities and locating drawbacks of GEC systems. Evaluating systems by combining these aspects also leads to superior human consistency over other reference-based and reference-less metrics. Extensive experiments on two human judgment datasets and six reference datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our method, achieving a new state-of-the-art result. Our codes are released at https://github.com/THUKElab/CLEME.

Furthermore, f VDB can process datasets with much larger footprint and spatial resolution than prior works, while providing a competitive memory footprint on small inputs. Simplicits: Mesh-Free, Geometry-Agnostic Elastic Simulation
papers.abstract: The proliferation of 3D representations, from explicit meshes to implicit neural fields and more, motivates the need for simulators agnostic to representation. We present a data-, mesh-, and grid-free solution for elastic simulation for any object in any geometric representation undergoing large, nonlinear deformations. We note that every standard geometric representation can be reduced to an occupancy function queried at any point in space, and we define a simulator atop this common interface. For each object, we fit a small implicit neural network encoding spatially varying weights that act as a reduced deformation basis. These weights are trained to learn physically significant motions in the object via random perturbations. alternate_titles: Path-space Differentiable Rendering of Implicit Surfaces
Path-Space Differentiable Rendering of Implicit Surfaces
papers.abstract: Physics-based differentiable rendering is a key ingredient for integrating forward rendering into probabilistic inference and machine learning pipelines. As a state-of-the-art formulation for differentiable rendering, differential path integrals have enabled the development of efficient Monte Carlo estimators for both interior and boundary integrals. Unfortunately, this formulation has been designed mostly for explicit geometries like polygonal meshes.

papers.title: SuperPADL: Scaling Language-Directed Physics-Based Control with Progressive Supervised Distillation
alternate_titles: SuperPADL: Scaling Language-Directed Physics-Based Control with Progressive Supervised Distillation
papers.abstract: Physically-simulated models for human motion can generate high-quality responsive character animations, often in real-time. Natural language serves as a flexible interface for controlling these models, allowing expert and non-expert users to quickly create and edit their animations. Many recent physics-based animation methods, including those that use text interfaces, train control policies using reinforcement learning (RL). However, scaling these methods beyond several hundred motions has remained challenging.

alternate_titles: Signatures Meet Dynamic Programming: Generalizing Bellman Equations for Trajectory Following
papers.abstract: Path signatures have been proposed as a powerful representation of paths that efficiently captures the path’s analytic and geometric characteristics, having useful algebraic properties including fast concatenation of paths through tensor products. Signatures have recently been widely adopted in machine learning problems for time series analysis. In this work we establish connections between value functions typically used in optimal control and intriguing properties of path signatures.
